name: Matelea

project_scope.note: The source pool preserves older Matelea usage. Current learner organization keeps only M. edwardsensis and M. reticulata in Matelea; former M. biflora is canonical Chthamalia biflora, and legacy M. gonocarpos maps to an unresolved Gonolobus suberosus var. granulatus concept.

priority: reticulate versus longitudinal or uniform corolla markings
growth form: low hairy herb versus vigorous twiner
study_strategy.warning: Do not treat every historical 'Matelea' record as the same modern genus concept. In this local set, M. biflora is Chthamalia biflora and legacy M. gonocarpos points to a Gonolobus concept that remains range/taxon-concept HOLD.

quick_key.then: Chthamalia biflora — source name Matelea biflora

look_here_first: On a milkvine with opposite heart-shaped leaves, FIND ONE OPEN FLOWER and inspect the flower face. Flat, strongly net-veined green petals plus bright silvery pearl = Matelea reticulata. Slightly bell-shaped flower with mainly lengthwise lines, hairy inside and raised fleshy corona segments = M. edwardsensis. Very small 5 mm green-white flowers in a many-flowered axillary spray = talayote, Cynanchum unifarium, a DIFFERENT genus. Large, uniformly olive-green star plus smoothly angled pod = Gonolobus, not Matelea.
shared_traits: Twining milkweed vines with opposite, often deeply cordate leaves, milky latex and paired follicles (a pair may develop from one flower); these traits also occur in related genera, so they are not diagnostic alone.
In the local comparison, evaluate corolla shape (rotate/flat vs campanulate/bell), surface pattern (reticulation vs longitudinal lines), INNER-SIDE hairs, corona architecture and follicle armature.
Do not classify by leaf shape alone. Look for the flower's fused gynostegium and pollinia as dogbane-family clues. Mature fruit may be crucial when a flower is absent.

comparison_cards.title: Pearl milkvine vs Edwards Plateau milkvine
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Face the open flower directly. Pearl milkvine is FLAT with a dense netted dark-green pattern and conspicuous silver center. Edwards Plateau milkvine is MORE BELL-SHAPED and marked primarily by lengthwise stripes. Side-angle then reveals the hairy inner corolla and fleshy lobed corona of edwardsensis.

field_matrix.reticulata: Heavy mesh-like dark reticulation over lobes
field_matrix.edwardsensis: Mostly parallel lengthwise marks; only distal tips/margins reticulate
Dense short hairs on inner corolla

field_matrix.reticulata: Highly reduced low corona, SILVERY anther appendages
field_matrix.edwardsensis: Clearly fleshy raised 5-lobed corona without conspicuous silver pearl

comparison_cards.caution: These co-occur on the eastern Edwards Plateau. Both climb with heart-shaped leaves and green flowers, so leaf-only IDs are unreliable.

comparison_cards.title: Talayote vs pearl/plateau milkvines
comparison_cards.look_here_first: First photograph an ENTIRE flower spray with a finger for scale. Talayote's many tiny ~5 mm green-with-white-rim flowers occur along a branched axillary cyme/raceme. Matelea milkvines instead have larger showy patterned corollas. For fruit, Talayote has a smooth plump pod versus rough/studded Matelea pods.

field_matrix.matelea: Much showier green corollas, patterns obvious to the eye
field_matrix.talayote: Small (~5 mm across) green flower with pale/white edged lobes

field_matrix.matelea: Smaller groups of larger flowers; inspect actual per-species peduncles
field_matrix.talayote: Often 10+ tiny flowers, spaced along a racemelike axillary cyme

field_matrix.matelea: Pearl vs Plateau: netted/flat vs longitudinal/bell
field_matrix.talayote: Fleshy 3-lobed corona hoods, small shallow bell-shaped green corolla
Plump smooth, ca. 7.5–9.5 cm x 3–3.3 cm
Short hairs commonly in a LINE along stem

comparison_cards.caution: Both can exude WHITE latex and have opposite heart-shaped leaves. Sap and leaf shape alone do NOT separate talayote from Matelea. Talayote can also resemble Gonolobus vegetatively.

comparison_cards.title: Pearl milkvine vs anglepod
comparison_cards.look_here_first: On a flowering vine, look for MESH PATTERN and SILVERY CENTRAL PEARL. If the green petals are uniform olive rather than netted, suspect anglepod. A mature fruit with sharp LONGITUDINAL ANGLES (but smooth skin) supports anglepod.

field_matrix.matelea: Dark green netting across nearly round petals

comparison_cards.caution: Legacy Matelea gonocarpos records are not the same as M. reticulata. Preserve the current Gonolobus variety identity and its existing range decision.

visual_comparison.title: Local milkvines: flower faces FIRST
visual_comparison.subtitle: Real photographs: preserve existing Joey Santore frames for pearl milkvine; compare with Edwards Plateau milkvine. Talayote original-site photo references are linked below, not substituted with another species.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: MESH + PEARL = M. reticulata; PARALLEL LINES + HAIRY BELL = M. edwardsensis; TINY GREEN-WHITE SPRAYS + SMOOTH POD = Cynanchum talayote; UNIFORM OLIVE + ANGLED POD = Gonolobus.
